newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Italy say Albanian elections must go ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Italy say Albanian elections must go ahead.

text.p: The United States and Italy agreed on Friday that general elections in Albania must go ahead as planned next week despite violence, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said.

"We are in any event convinced that the situation in two to three months' time would not be very different. So let's go ahead with the elections," Dini told Reuters after meeting U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright ahead of the Group of Seven summit here.
"We are in full agreement that we must go ahead with the elections on June 29," he said.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in Albania this year and about 50 have died in the past week as the election campaign draws to a close.
President Sali Berisha was forced in March to agree to an early election after law and order broke down when pyramid investment schemes in which many Albanians had put their life savings collapsed.

His Democratic Party is defending a big parliamentary majority won in last year's polls and denounced as unfair by both Albania's opposition and Western observers. Berisha is not running for reelection.
Italy is leading a 7,000-strong multinational peacekeeping force in Albania.
Dini said Albania would continue to receive international assistance if the government pursued acceptable policies.
"The European Union and the international community intends to help if they agree to follow reasonable policies," he said.
